text:
nima: quick q — we've been benchmarking two collector topologies: a single consolidated gateway that handles spans+metrics+logs per-tenant vs lightweight per-signal pipelines on the agent. Observing 20-40% lower p50 for tail-heavy apps with per-signal. thinking about a default recommendation and console UX to let teams opt-in. anyone have strong take on tradeoffs?
jordan: +1 for per-signal for high-throughput tenants. consolidated gateway reduces deployment footprint but increases mem/CPU and KV-cache pressure for long-lived spans. also harder to enforce per-signal retention.
liz: agree. consolidated simplifies ops and routing rules, though. for small customers it's cheaper. main concern is exporter connection churn in per-agent mode — more outbound connections.
rohit: exporter churn can be mitigated with connection pooling + multiplexing proxy at gateway. we already have proto for multiplex header. performance wise the big win is smaller kv caches per-signal which reduces cache misses for long traces.
sara: from console/UX side, we need three things: a) per-route retention overrides in a compact view b) a cost estimate widget (egress + tokenized retention) c) an easy toggle to switch topology per-tenant w/ rollout controls.
ops-bot: deploybot: new canary rollout created for "collector-topology-toggle" for tenant: acct-534, 10% traffic, started 2024-11-21T14:12:03Z
nima: here's a config example i sketched for per-signal pipelines (YAML):
```
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, tail_sampling]
      exporters: [tokio-multiplex-proxy]
    metrics:
      receivers: [prometheus]
      processors: [memory_limiter]
      exporters: [prom-mux]
```
rohit: nice. for consolidated we had a single pipeline and then a router processor that split by signal — lighter on connections but heavier process-level memory.
jordan: operationally we should gate per-tenant default on peak rps and unique-span-cardinality. maybe a short heuristics doc and an API: `POST /tenants/{id}/collector-config` to override.
liz: also flag: retention changes should be non-disruptive. when lowering retention, ensure we prune background indexes without blocking ingestion.
sara: UX rollout idea: show a "Suggested topology" banner in tenant settings with expected 7-day cost delta and a one-click canary opt-in. add a tiny sparklines panel per-signal for p50/p95.
rohit: telemetry-wise include a synthetic trace that goes through both topologies during canary to compare KV cache hit, exporter RTT, and CPU. bake those into the rollout evaluation.
nima: action items: 1) rohit + eng-runtime to draft connection pooling + mux proxy approach (PR by EOD Thu) 2) product/console (sara) to mock a "Suggested topology" tile + cost calc 3) eng-platform (liz/jordan) to document heuristics and API for per-tenant override 4) set up canary with synthetic traces and metrics.
sara: will mock wireframe and cost formula. keeping it minimal for first pass.
liz: i'll start docs for heuristics and add a short checklist for safe retention changes.
rohit: i'll prototype mux proxy and a small k6 test to simulate 10k rps mixed signals.
jordan: if we do per-signal as default for >X rps, need playbooks for rollback when exporter failures spike.
nima: cool — i'll track in the cadence doc. if anyone wants to join pairing for the PR ping me. :thumbsup:
